papers.title: Some Expressions involving Bernoulli, Harmonic, and Stirling Numbers
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several identities involving Bernoulli numbers, harmonic numbers, and Stirling numbers. Our approach extends the method developed by Kargin and Mutluer.

papers.title: Packaging Systems: Intrinsic Structure, Recovery Ranks, and Globalization Theorems
papers.abstract:
We define packaged structures through carriers, internal units, incidence, candidate spaces, and selected families. A realized packaging system additionally retains a context and formation datum related to its output by a possibly partial, multivalued realization relation. We establish comparison-relative recoverability and non-collapse criteria and an intrinsic refinement-completion theory. For atlas specializations, exact extension becomes a specialization-relative packaging completion problem. Under additional recovery and elimination axioms, we establish general globalization sufficiency criteria and sharp classifications for three classes of compatible finite atlases on a fixed cover $\mathcal H$. A geometric obstruction rank $
u(\mathcal H)$ yields thresholds $2k+1<
u(\mathcal H)$ for empty-preserving closures of local Carath'eodory number at most $k\ge1$; $d<
u(\mathcal H)$ for complete functional-dependency theories of local minimum Armstrong size at most $d\ge3$; and $3<
u(\mathcal H)$ for transitive relations, including equivalence relations. For nonempty finite label sets and empty-preserving closures, minimum commutant realization dimension equals minimum Armstrong size. We also determine intrinsic recovery ranks and construct canonical clique completions under bounded conformality without chordality. Explicit obstructions establish sharpness; a transport hypothesis is essential for the general recovery--obstruction converse. Complexity bounds apply locally, not necessarily to global extensions.

papers.title: A new family of deformed trigonometric functions and their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations: application to the nonlinear harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: In this work we present an extension of the classical trigonometric functions which include, amongst others, the Lindqvist p-trigonometric functions. Additionally, we show their relevance in the study of certain versions of the nonlinear harmonic oscillator equation. Furthermore, we study their more important mathematical properties and obtain their corresponding Pythagorean-like relations. We also define a new extension of the Beta and Ateb sine functions using these new $\chi$-trigonometric functions. Indeed, these new Beta and Ateb functions are involved in the closed form expressions obtained for the solutions of the nonlinear oscillator under certain constraints.

papers.title: A new arrangement inequality (revised and extended version)
papers.abstract: We study the cyclic inequality \[ \sum_{i=1}^n x_i\,\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^a x_{i+1}^b\;\le\;\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^{(1+a+b)/2}\Big)^2, \] where $x_1,\dots,x_n\ge 0$ and indices are taken modulo $n$. Let $N(a,b)$ be the largest $n$ for which the inequality holds for all nonnegative $x_i$. We show that $N(a,b)$ is bounded above by an explicit quantity $N^*(a,b)$ obtained from the second variation at the constant vector, and we conjecture that $N(a,b)=N^*(a,b)$. For $a=b=1$ we prove that the inequality holds if and only if $n\le 8$, which settles the case left open in the original version of this paper. For $n=4$ the inequality holds whenever $1,a,b$ are the sides of a triangle, with an explicit remainder term. We show that $N$ is monotone along rays emanating from the line $a+b=1$; this corrects and extends an earlier monotonicity statement. Finally, any $n$ nonnegative numbers can be arranged so that the inequality holds; for $n\neq 6$ this is achieved by one of $n-1$ prescribed arrangements, which yields a volume bound for every such $n$.

papers.title: A systematic approach to Diophantine equations: two thousand solved examples
papers.abstract: Monograph "B. Grechuk, Polynomial Diophantine equations. A systematic approach" suggests solving Diophantine equations systematically in certain order. Many hundreds of the equations are left to the reader. Here, we provide complete solutions to all these equations. The difficulties of solved equations range from elementary to research level. In the last section, we present a summary table of all solved equations ordered by their size, which makes them easy to find. As a result, this document may be used as a database of solved Diophantine equations of small size, to which more difficult equations can be reduced.
